page: Vultr vcg-a40-24c-120g-48vram is a dedicated bare-metal GPU server type designed for compute workloads requiring hardware-accelerated processing and dedicated host resources. The platform is powered by a 2.0 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processor delivering 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated virtual execution threads. System memory totals 120.0 GB, providing an allocation of 5.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage includes a bundled 1400 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one pre-assigned public IPv4 address. Accelerated computing is driven by a single NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU equipped with 48 GB of dedicated VRAM.

Benchmark evaluations position the Intel Xeon processor within average tier margins across typical synthetic compute loads, recording a Geekbench multi-core result of 13941.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 35837.28. The host architecture demonstrates strong performance in uncached large-block memory read bandwidth at 192.56 GB/sec and Geekbench image processing at 14764.0. Instruction set flags include AVX-512 Foundation and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), enhancing integer operations for vector and neural network routines.

The 48 GB VRAM capacity of the NVIDIA A40 supports dedicated AI inference pipelines, reaching 1647.37 prompt processing tokens per second on lightweight 135M models and 45.06 tokens per second on 7B models. Hardware constraints become apparent when handling 70B parameter models, where prompt processing throughput drops to 4.33 tokens per second, indicating that scaling larger generative models necessitates multi-GPU topologies. The bundled NVMe storage and balanced memory-to-core ratio offer robust IOPS and caching capacity without requiring external storage attachments.

This hardware configuration is suited for AI inference across small-to-medium language models, image and video processing pipelines, ray tracing visualization, and GPU-accelerated database operations. The inclusion of dedicated host cores, high-capacity VRAM, and fast NVMe storage provides consistent execution for environments where virtualized resource sharing is undesirable.
